A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research and contain 60 readable pages, including Appendices A–G, Figures 1–32 and Tables 1–7. Text and rendered-page comparisons reveal no material gaps.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments training GPT-2 models on C4 and measuring membership inference, decision instability and extraction vulnerability in Sections 3–6 and Appendices B–F.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and their outcomes, including LiRA/RMIA comparisons and measurements of per-sample membership decision instability.

M1.justification: The attack procedures, GPT-2 architectures, observation statistics and calibrated membership-decision diagnostic remain unchanged in Sections 2–5 and Appendices A–B.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same C4 and deduplicated-C4 coverage, membership-inference and extraction tasks, and online/offline attack scenarios.

E2.justification: Appendix B retains the same comparisons involving LiRA, RMIA and RMIA (simple), including online/offline variants. The newly cited work is not an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Data subsampling, model sizes, training budgets, reference-model counts, evaluation metrics and extraction procedures are unchanged, including the configurations in Appendix G and Table 7.

E4.justification: The reference-count, observation-statistic, learning-rate, duplication, overtraining and per-sample vulnerability analyses are retained without revisions in Appendices B–F.

E5.justification: The 16-run experiments, 125/127-target instability studies, mean and standard-deviation reporting, and exact binomial tests and cutoffs remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings match throughout the figures and tables. For example, Figure 2 retains the 85M model's AUC of 0.699, and Figure 5 retains AUC 0.752 ± 0.007 for the 302M study.

T1.justification: The MIA formulas, flip-rate definition, unbiased estimator and binomial acceptance-band derivations remain unchanged in Appendices A and E.2.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same four findings concerning attack success, practical performance limits, per-sample instability and relationships to other privacy metrics.

C2.justification: Appendix E.2.7 already distinguishes descriptive from inferential claims in v2; v3 only adds a citation to that passage. Interpretations, mechanism explanations and limitations otherwise remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproducibility information is unchanged, including NanoDO usage, preprocessing, optimizer settings and the experimental configurations in Appendix G and Table 7.

R1.justification: v3 adds Chouldechova et al. (2025), 'Comparison requires valid measurement: Rethinking attack success rate comparisons in AI red teaming,' as reference [9], cited in Appendix E.2.7. Previous references and broader research positioning are retained.

P1.justification: The displayed author name changes from 'Adam Dziedic' to 'Adam Dziedzic'. Citation numbers and the arXiv version/date stamp are updated, without substantive rewriting or section reorganization.

P2.justification: The added reference produces limited bibliography reflow across pages 11–15, with small paragraph reflows elsewhere. Figures and tables retain their placement, structure, axes and legends.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects an author-name typo and adds a supporting citation to an existing distinction in Appendix E.2.7. These small attribution edits leave the scientific evidence, reasoning, reproducibility and substantive exposition unchanged, producing no meaningful overall quality difference.
